Chapter 9: Building a Counter-Culture—Living Faithfully in a Humanistic World.
It’s one thing to spot how humanism shapes the world around us. But living in a way that stands out, that’s a whole different challenge, isn’t it? For most of us, it’s not just about having the right beliefs—it’s about creating a life, and a community, that actually reflects what we believe.
Picture this: a group of friends, fed up with shallow connections and surface-level faith, decide to do something new. Instead of simply meeting for a Bible study, they gather to share meals, help their neighbors, and genuinely support each other through all the ups and downs of life.
They wanted their faith to be more than just words—something that would shape every part of their lives.
Now, I’ll be honest, at first it felt awkward. They were all used to keeping things light, steering clear of tough conversations, and hiding their struggles. But as they started opening up, everything began to shift. They discovered freedom in honesty, strength in being vulnerable, and a real sense of hope that came from sharing a purpose.
Slowly, these changes started showing up in everyday life. At work, they looked for ways to serve instead of competing. Within their families, they practiced forgiveness and patience. And in their neighborhoods, they reached out to folks who were lonely or hurting.
The truth is, most of us underestimate the power of community. We might think faith is something private, just between us and God. But the early church had a different idea. They knew that real transformation happens in relationship—with God, and with each other.
What made this group’s commitment special wasn’t anything flashy or dramatic. They didn’t set out to change the world overnight. Instead, they focused on showing up, telling the truth, and loving well—those small, faithful acts that really add up. And over time, their community became a beacon of hope, a place where people could actually feel the love of God in real, tangible ways.
So, what does it look like to live faithfully in a humanistic world? It’s not about withdrawing, or pointing fingers. It’s about building a new kind of culture—one marked by humility, generosity, and courage. It’s about showing the world there is another way to live, one that leads to life.
